title: Bucketed KV delta-checkpointing and soft-tenant OOM strategy for blocked/paged residency
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Problem: As we push more multi-tenant workloads into Dedicated and Private deployments with large context models, the paged/blocked KV cache frequently triggers hard OOMs on GPUs when hotset spikes overlap across tenants. Continuous batching amplifies transient working set concurrency, causing eviction storms and high tail latency.

Goal: Implement a bucketed delta-checkpointing scheme combined with a soft-tenant OOM strategy that: (1) lets the KV system checkpoint and reclaim small dirty deltas to host memory in bucketed batches, (2) enforces per-tenant soft residency budgets with graceful degradation (throttles batching or spills to CPU) before hard OOM, and (3) cooperates with the runtime scheduler to prioritize low-latency in-flight requests during eviction/restore cycles.

Scope: Design and prototype within the serving runtime (C++ core + CUDA paths + host async threads) and expose knobs via the allocator config. Integration with console telemetry and rollout-controlled defaults is in-scope for Beta release.
acceptance_criteria:
- No hard GPU OOMs in simulated multi-tenant stress tests (10 tenants, 2 large-context models each) for 30 minutes of mixed traffic.
- 95th percentile token latency for in-flight requests increases by <=15% during eviction/restore cycles.
- Checkpoint/writeback throughput of deltas supports reclaim rate >= 1.2x incoming hotset growth in stress tests.
- End-to-end unit + integration tests added and passing in CI.
- Config knobs added: bucket_size_bytes, per_tenant_soft_quota_bytes, async_writeback_parallelism.
implementation_notes:
Design summary:
1) Bucketed delta-checkpointing: Partition KV blocks into fixed-size buckets (default 8MB) aligned to GPU page boundaries. Track a per-bucket dirty bitmap representing modified lanes. When reclaim triggers, aggregate small dirty ranges into a single host writeback operation using pinned buffers to minimize PCIe overhead.
2) Micro-residency tiers: Maintain 3 residency tiers per tenant: HOT (pinned GPU), WARM (host-prefetched, easy to promote), COLD (on host only). Promote/demote uses token-affinity heatmaps sampled at the request dispatcher.
3) Soft-tenant quotas: Each tenant has a soft_budget that is enforced by a reclamation oracle. When over budget, the system first raises async writeback for oldest buckets, then applies light-weight request-level throttles (backpressure on batching window) and finally marks non-critical sequences for host spill.
4) Cooperative eviction: The request scheduler communicates in-flight token ranges to the KV controller so eviction avoids currently referenced cache lanes. Scheduler exposes a short-lived lease (50-200ms) per batch so eviction can skip or delay buckets.
5) Writeback throttling: Use congestion-aware writeback that adapts number of concurrent cudaMemcpyAsync streams based on observed P2P saturation and end-to-end latency.

Data structures & algorithms:
- BucketIndex: uint32 bucket_id -> metadata {last_touched_ts, dirty_bitmap_base64, tenant_id, residency_tier}.
- EvictionScore = alpha * age_score + beta * coldness + gamma * tenant_pressure - delta * batch_lease_score. Tunable weights; default alpha=1.0,beta=1.2,gamma=2.0,delta=3.0.
- Checkpoint coalescer: squashes contiguous dirty lanes into up to N scatter-gather segments (N default 16) per bucket to limit host write syscall pressure.

Runtime integration:
- New async host writeback worker pool (configurable threads).
- Expose telemetry metrics: kv.bucket.writeback.bytes, kv.bucket.writeback.latency_p50/p95, kv.residency.tenantX.gpu_bytes, kv.eviction.score_histogram.
- Add gRPC RPCs for the console to fetch soft_quota and eviction events for audit/alerts.

progress_updates:
2026-01-20: Initial prototype of dirty-bitmap packing completed; landed local helper utilities (PR #4928).
2026-01-28: BucketIndex schema reviewed with storage team; changed bucket_size default from 4MB -> 8MB to reduce writeback frequency after microbenching.
2026-02-03: Host writeback worker skeleton implemented; pinned-buffer pool and async queueing in place. Observed 30% PCIe transfer batching improvement in microbench.
2026-02-08: Scheduler lease API implemented; integration test shows eviction skipping batches with active leases. Still tuning lease timeout to avoid starvation.
2026-02-12: Began multi-tenant stress harness runs; first pass prevented OOMs for 10m but hit higher p95 latency during peak writeback. Next: tune writeback parallelism and eviction weights.
decisions:
- Use fixed-size buckets (8MB) to simplify alignment with GPU page granularity and reduce fragmentation risk.
- Represent dirty bitmap as compressed base64 string in metadata for lighter cross-process IPC.
- Default soft-tenant quota is 75% of tenant committed reservation; overcommit handled via tiered demotion.
- No immediate change to on-disk persistence semantics; writeback is solely for host-residency reclaim (no persistence guarantee).
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Writeback saturates PCIe and spikes request latency. Mitigation: implement congestion-aware stream scaler and limit concurrent writebacks based on observed latency headroom.
- Risk: Composite eviction score tuning might starve small tenants. Mitigation: add fairness floor and a periodic fairness pass that promotes under-served tenants.
- Risk: Leases add complexity to scheduler and could cause delayed reclaim. Mitigation: short default leases (100ms) and a hard reclaim override when free memory below critical threshold.
test_plan:
- Unit: bitmap packing/unpacking, bucket coalescer segmentation logic.
- Integration: end-to-end promote/demote flows with simulated request dispatcher and batch leases.
- Stress: 10 tenant mixed traffic run for 30m (varying context lengths and burstiness) with metrics recorded.
- Fault injection: drop writeback completion callbacks to ensure recovery and re-promote logic functions.
- Performance regression: validate p50/p95 token latency vs baseline under continuous batching (target <= +15% p95).
